column1: # MOOSE 3.2 class -> UBERON crosswalk for the CT-derived atlas (D5, D7b).
# Hand-built and hand-checked on 27 July 2026. Every `uberon` CURIE in this file
# was verified by fetching the term back from EBI OLS4 and comparing the
# ontology's own label against `uberon_label` below — see
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AND CANNOT BE GENERATED
# MOOSE ships a SNOMED-CT mapping (moosez/mappings/SNOMED.py). It does not join
# to UBERON: it uses SNOMED *structure* concepts while UBERON cross-references
# SNOMED *entire* concepts, so the join returns zero rows. Verified previously
# and recorded in docs/PHOTOREALISM_AND_PERSONALISATION.md 5.4. This table is
# the manual bridge, and it is the real integration cost of the CT pipeline.
#   moose_model   MOOSE model that emits the class
#   moose_class   the class name in that model's dataset.json (authoritative)
#   uberon        UBERON CURIE, or empty when no term exists (see status=flag)
#   uberon_label  the ontology's own rdfs:label, verbatim, for the check above
#   layer         our closed AnatomyLayer set (src/store.ts): organ|connective|muscle|bone
#   side          left|right|"" — needed because UBERON often has no lateral term
#   status        ok | flag  (flag = a human has to decide something here)
#                 A flag is a REVIEW marker, not an exclusion. labelmap2glb.py
#                 ships flagged rows by default with a per-structure warning,
#                 because dropping the spleen out of an anatomical atlas over an
#                 unsettled system assignment is the wrong failure. Use --strict
#                 to exclude them. Rows with an EMPTY uberon column are excluded
#                 by default regardless, since they cannot join to anything.
#   note          why, when it is not obvious
# NODE-NAME COLLISIONS ARE EXPECTED AND HANDLED
# UBERON's laterality coverage is patchy: it has left/right terms for kidney,
# adrenal and clavicle, and none for femur, humerus, scapula, rib or hip bone.
# So `femur_left` and `femur_right` legitimately share UBERON:0000981. The GLB
# builder disambiguates the glTF node name as `UBERON_0000981.left` — the dot is
# deliberate: AtlasBody's CURIE regex needs a NON-word character after the
# digits, so `UBERON_0000981_left` would fail to parse and `.left` parses.
# The unambiguous ontology term always also travels in extras.ontologyid.
# SYSTEM ASSIGNMENTS FOLLOW THE PROJECT'S EXISTING CONVENTION, NOT A TEXTBOOK
# Taken from docs/bodyparts3d-system-map.tsv and src/scene/anatomy/layout.ts so
# the CT atlas colours the same way the BodyParts3D atlas already does:
# liver / pancreas / gallbladder / kidney / urinary bladder -> metabolic,
# ⚠️ Those two existing files DISAGREE about kidney (layout.ts says endocrine,
# the manifest says metabolic). This file follows the manifest, because the
# manifest is what actually drives the shipped atlas. Worth reconciling.

column9: note
MOOSE says "bladder"; the class is the urinary bladder, not the gallbladder.

UBERON term is certain; the SYSTEM is a judgement call. The spleen is a lymphoid/haematological organ and our closed set has no lymphatic id. cardiovascular is the least-wrong home (blood filtration); metabolic is the other defensible answer. Needs the same named reviewer the scoring weights need.
MOOSE segments the two lobes separately; UBERON has per-lobe terms, so this is exact rather than a shared-term case.
Present in the shipped dataset.json but MISSING from the ENHANCE.PET bucket's labels.json. Trust dataset.json.

layer is deliberately organ, not muscle: AtlasBody treats layer=muscle as an outer skeletal-muscle shell with its own visibility toggle, so tagging the heart wall as muscle would hide the heart whenever muscles are hidden.
UBERON has left/right terms for the iliac ARTERY but not the iliac VEIN. Both sides share the unsided term; the side column and the node-name suffix carry laterality.
See iliac_vena_left.

MOOSE merges TWO distinct vessels into one class. UBERON has no union term: hepatic portal vein is UBERON:0001639 and splenic vein is UBERON:0003713. Shipping it as the portal vein alone is a factual overstatement of what the mask contains. Either split the mask geometrically or label the node "portal and splenic vein" with no single CURIE.
Autochthon is the continental-radiology name for the intrinsic (deep) back muscles; the erector spinae group is the accepted equivalent and is what the mask actually covers.
Note the IDs are NOT in the order you would guess: maximus is ...370 and medius is ...371. Do not extrapolate UBERON ids.
UBERON's label is generic but its synonyms include "C1 vertebra" and "atlas"; there is no term literally called "cervical vertebra 1".
Synonyms include "C2 vertebra" and "axis".
⚠️ T8 breaks the numeric run. T1-T7 are 0004626-0004632 and T9-T12 resume at 0004633; T8 sits at 0011050. Extrapolating the range gives the WRONG bone for T8 through T12.

NO UBERON TERM EXISTS. A sixth lumbar vertebra is a transitional-anatomy variant (lumbarised S1). Rare, and absent in most subjects. Do not invent a CURIE. Either drop the class or emit the node with ontologyid empty and a plain label.
MOOSE's "hip" is the hip BONE (os coxa), not the joint. UBERON has no lateral term.
fused sacrum is UBERON's label; "sacrum" and "os sacrum" are its synonyms.
⚠️ Same discontinuity as T8: rib 8 is 0010757, NOT 0004608 (which is rib 9).
NO UBERON TERM. A 13th rib is not standard human anatomy; the class exists because the label set was drawn up to tolerate variants. Expect it to be empty in almost every scan. Do not invent a CURIE.
See rib_left_13.
The bone HRA-male lacks entirely (D7b). This row is a large part of why the CT route exists.
One mask for all eight carpals, so the term is the generic "carpal bone" rather than a named bone.
MOOSE's "fingers" is a BONE class in a bones model — the phalanges, not the soft-tissue digit (which would be UBERON:0002389 manual digit).

One mask for the whole cranium and mandible. ⚠️ This is also the privacy-critical structure: a skull surface plus soft tissue is a reconstructible face. See docs/PHOTOREALISM_AND_PERSONALISATION.md 5.5 before shipping it from real patient data.
As with fingers: the bone, not the soft-tissue digit.

MOOSE's small_bowel excludes the duodenum, which it emits separately; UBERON:0002108 includes it. Slight over-claim, kept because splitting it would need a term for "jejunum and ileum" that UBERON does not have as a single class.

REGION MASK, not an anatomical structure — the trunk envelope. Deliberately NOT UBERON:0002097 (skin of body): that would claim a tissue the mask does not delineate. UBERON:0002100 (trunk) is honest about what it is, a body region, and matches how head/arms/legs are handled below. Together the four are the integumentary hull, which AtlasBody already renders semi-transparent under the user's hullOpacity control.

Region mask, and the right term for the region, but the mesh is an envelope rather than an organ. ⚠️ Also the defacing surface — a head envelope derived from real patient imaging is biometric data under GDPR Art. 4(14); do not ship it. See PHOTOREALISM_AND_PERSONALISATION.md 5.5.
Region mask, BOTH arms in one label, while UBERON:0001460 is singular "arm". One node cannot honestly be one arm; this needs either a geometric split or a plural label.
Region mask, both legs in one label. Same singular/plural problem as arms.
Tissue class, not a named muscle: one mask covering all skeletal muscle in the field of view. Useful as a volume statistic, poor as a selectable structure.

UBERON term is exact. The SYSTEM is arguable: subcutaneous fat sits in the hypodermis, which is why integumentary is defensible, but metabolic is the system a body-composition score would actually feed. Pick one deliberately.
The body-composition signal with the strongest clinical evidence behind it (D5a).
